description:
Current provider registration (\`Application.get_env(:octo_pi_ai, :providers) |> Map.put(...) |> Application.put_env/3\`) races under concurrent app start — the moment OpenAI/Google apps land and boot in parallel with Anthropic, one provider's merge stomps another.

RESEARCH.md §5 already specifies this seam: \"OctoPi.AI.ProviderRegistry (ETS owner).\"

Create OctoPi.AI.ProviderRegistry under OctoPi.AI.Application's supervisor. Provides:
- register(api :: atom, module)
- lookup(api) :: module | nil
- list() :: %{atom => module}

Uses a public, named ETS table (read_concurrency: true). Each provider's Application.start/2 calls ProviderRegistry.register(:anthropic_messages, OctoPi.AI.Providers.Anthropic) instead of the current Application.put_env dance.

Core OctoPi.AI.stream/3 reads via ProviderRegistry.lookup instead of Application.get_env.

TDD:
- RED: test \"two apps calling ProviderRegistry.register concurrently don't lose registrations\" (use Task.async pair).
- RED: test \"lookup returns module after register\", \"lookup returns nil for unknown api\".
- GREEN: implement the GenServer-owned ETS table.
- REGRESSION: existing ai_stream_test and mix ai.demo still work.

Files: new apps/octo_pi_ai/lib/octo_pi/ai/provider_registry.ex + test; ai.ex (switch to lookup); anthropic/application.ex (switch to register call).
title: Provider registry: ETS-owned dispatch table instead of Application.put_env
